questions.q: What did the noise experiment show about the useless panic button?
a: People with a button endured more noise than those without one
People pressed the button constantly and gave up sooner
The button made the noise feel louder
Only people told about the button used it
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the button did nothing, yet the group that had it withstood much more noise.

questions.q: Why can bringing a more attractive friend to a club hurt your chances?
a: The comparison makes you look less attractive than you are
Your friend receives all the attention you wanted
Strangers assume you are already taken
Groups are less likely to approach pairs
questions.why: Lesson 2 uses this example to introduce the contrast effect, where we judge by comparison.

questions.q: How does the contrast effect make discounts work?
a: We compare the new price with the old one instead of judging real value
We assume a higher price always means better quality
We trust shops that offer frequent sales
We prefer products that are almost sold out
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that a $70 item seems better at $70 off $100 than one normally priced at $70.

questions.q: What happened when the jelly display shrank from 24 kinds to six?
a: Ten times more jelly was sold
Sales dropped because shoppers had fewer options
Shoppers spent longer deciding what to buy
The same amount was sold either way
questions.why: Lesson 3 reports that the smaller display sold ten times as much as the larger one.
